c1.note: Raycon is private and Raycon Global Inc. is the entity, which is correct, but the claim never names the owner (GoDigital Media Group since March 2024).

c4.note: Raycon announced on March 19, 2024 that GoDigital Media Group had acquired it, so Ray Lee and management do not control it. The revenuememo claim is unsupported, and its own page admits no confirmed ownership data. All variants (F, C, D) are false.

c5.note: The acquisition by GoDigital Media Group contradicts Lee-and-management control. Only the part saying Ray J holds no equity is right.

c6.note: Acquisition terms and price were not publicly disclosed. The wording about 'remaining shareholders' is slightly off given the GoDigital acquisition.

c9.note: The page says public details about the acquisition price and terms have not been disclosed.

c11.note: The release is dated March 6, 2024 and says exactly this.

c13.note: The release names Tronix Network as Ray J's new television venture.

c16.note: Founding in 2017 by Ray J and Ray Lee, New York base and the name blend are all supported; this is background, not current ownership.

c17.note: BGR confirms the founders and their roles.

c18.note: The 2024 release quotes Ray Lee as Raycon CEO, and Revenue Memo calls him CEO in 2026.

c19.note: Revenue Memo and BrandsOwnedBy support Lee as CEO with a stake and control, but the GoDigital claim conflicts, so confidence is medium.

c20.note: Lee is named CEO in the March 2024 release and is still described as CEO in 2026 sources.

c22.note: Revenue Memo reports no disclosed outside investors, though the GoDigital report would contradict this if it holds.

c23.note: Revenue Memo says there are no confirmed outside investors and the only outside capital was an unverified 2017 distribution deal.

c25.note: LegalClarity (June 12, 2026) does say this and says terms were undisclosed, though the underlying claim is uncorroborated.

c27.note: LegalClarity gives the self-description and Wikipedia says the group was founded by Jason Peterson.

c28.note: GoDigital's about page and homepage do not mention Raycon, so no primary source confirms the acquisition.

c29.note: The Wikipedia subsidiary list does not include Raycon.

c30.note: Black Enterprise reports the $35-45M to $85-100M estimates and no figure was officially disclosed.

c31.note: Black Enterprise says Ray J exited 'despite its $300 million in revenue, The Jasmine Brand reported'; the attribution is accurate, though the figure is unverified.

c32.note: BGR says the deal 'potentially brought in up to $100 million'; the Jasmine Brand reported $80-100M. The figure is an unconfirmed estimate and the claim is hedged as such.

c33.note: The page names RAVI LLC (Delaware) as majority holder, with Cowboy Wholesale and Ray Lee holding minority stakes and no percentages given; the claim describes the page accurately, though the page itself is low-reliability.

c34.note: Black Enterprise reports estimates ranging from 61% to 30-40%, and Revenue Memo repeats the 30-61% range.

c35.note: The page says Ray J co-founded Raycon with Cowboy Wholesale executives and also lists Cowboy Wholesale as a minority owner, while legalclarity says Cowboy was no longer a partner by 2021. This supports the unreliability claim.

c24.note: The primary release says Ray J's shares were bought back by the company in March 2024, and it names no GoDigital acquisition.
